doc: Automated looking and critique of a delivered MP4's picture, the visual twin of ears. Every check reports a measured value, pass / warn / fail against the pack spec (or a stated house default) and a concrete fix with timestamps. It measures; it does not replace one human look at phone size.
deps: numpy, scipy, ffmpeg (decode). Pillow only in the tests (synthetic frames and text). Nothing is downloaded and no model is used.

eyes/frame0.doc: frame 0 is not black or near-uniform, the first visible change lands by frame 6 (never later than 0.5 s), and the frame has a readable subject (centre-surround saliency region against its surround, WCAG ratio)
eyes/frame0.source: SKILL.md banned defaults (a black frame 0; first visible change by frame 6) + VIRALITY checklist (hook) + frame-design (one high-contrast hero, 3:1)

eyes/frames.doc: black, empty (near-uniform) and frozen runs after frame 0 that the plan does not call a hold or a dip, a black tail, and playback stalls (a timestamp gap over 1.5 frames)
eyes/frames.source: SKILL.md VIRALITY (something visible changes at least every 3.5 s; trim a dead last 1-2 s) + production gate 3 (stills) + plan.shots[].hold

eyes/flashes.doc: WCAG 2.3.1 general flash (pair of opposing luminance changes of 10% or more where the darker side is under 0.80, over 25% of the screen) and red flash, counted in any 1 s window
eyes/flashes.source: SKILL.md QA checklist (flash safety, at most 3 per second) + references/gotchas.md (flash and photosensitivity) + WCAG 2.x 2.3.1

eyes/banding.doc: 8-bit posterisation of smooth gradients after the encode: staircases of long one-step luma plateaus on sampled native-resolution frames, with the region and the fix (grain or dither, encode settings)
eyes/banding.source: references/gotchas.md (meshGradient bands without grain, keep grain at 0.02 or more) + frame-design looks and grain (upload-safe stock)

eyes/safezones.doc: with a plan that names text boxes: every box against the platform safe rectangle; without one: persistent high-contrast text-like edge blocks inside the platform's unsafe bands
eyes/safezones.source: type/safezones.js lintRect + references/platforms.md (9:16 conservative rectangle, per-preset fractions) + frame-design (faces and key text stay out of the bottom 35%)

eyes/readability.doc: per on-screen text: rendered size at the 1080 reference and on a 360 px phone against the frame-design floors, time on screen against the reading speed (0.35 s + 0.28 s per word), the hook text start, and the WCAG contrast measured from the decoded pixels behind it (worst sampled frame)
eyes/readability.source: skills/frame-design/SKILL.md size table and reading time + references/type-and-color.md section 4 (WCAG 1.4.3 / 1.4.11) + type/safezones.js lintCaptionStyle

eyes/pacing.doc: hard cuts per minute (scene detection), shot length median and average, shots per 30 s, and the longest static hold, against the plan's format (cuts/patterns.json pace) and the 3.5 s rule
eyes/pacing.source: cuts/patterns.json pace + templates/_shared/plan.mjs lintPace (paceRule) + references/virality.md interrupt ladder + SKILL.md VIRALITY (a visible change at least every 3.5 s)

eyes/composition.doc: one hero per key frame (saliency blobs that compete with the strongest), letterbox or pillarbox bars that the plan did not ask for, aspect and resolution against the platform
eyes/composition.source: frame-design (one hero per frame; re-layout, never crop) + references/platforms.md + templates/_shared/plan.mjs PLATFORMS and SIZES + skills/social-video (1080 x 1920 masters)

eyes/encode.doc: codec, profile, yuv420p, faststart (moov before mdat), colour tags, keyframe interval, bits per pixel and a blockiness proxy (8 / 16 px grid steps against the rest)
eyes/encode.source: skills/social-video/SKILL.md (H.264 High, yuv420p, faststart) + skills/motion-stack/references/output-tools.md (moov before mdat, bt709 tags) + SKILL.md QA (Files: CRF 23, a few MB)

analysis.note: frames are area-scaled to this long side for the per-frame numbers (flash, freeze, cuts, saliency); banding, bars, blockiness, text contrast and text edges read native-resolution frames

platforms.note: presets and safezones are copied from templates/_shared/plan.mjs (PLATFORMS, SIZES) and type/safezones.js (SAFE); eyes/tests fail when they drift. Every per-platform safe zone is a working estimate (verify: true in safezones.js): look at the current apps before a paid campaign

frame0.note: levels are 0-255 on the decoded luma of an area-scaled frame. Black = mean at or under 16 and std under 6. A visible change = 0.5% of the pixels moved 16 levels, or the mean moved 1.5 levels, against frame 0. The subject is the spot with the strongest centre-surround response (difference of Gaussians, sigma 1.2% and 9% of the long side); the WCAG ratio between the 85th and 15th luminance percentile in a window of 9% radius around it must reach 3:1 (frame-design: meaningful graphics), 1.5:1 warns

frames.note: frozen = consecutive frames that differ by under 0.15 level (mean, area-scaled): a duplicated or stalled picture, not a slow move. A frozen or empty run the plan does not mark (shots[].hold, plan.holds, audio.quiet kind hold) warns from 0.5 s and fails from 1.0 s. Without a plan a freeze that runs to the last frame and is at most 4.5 s long (the end-card fine print is held 3-4.5 s) is a note. A dip to black the plan names (a shot whose tx has dip, plan.black) is not a fault

flashes.note: WCAG 2.x 2.3.1: a general flash is a pair of opposing changes in relative luminance of 0.10 or more where the darker image is under 0.80, over a quarter of the screen; more than 3 in any 1 s fails. The red flash uses a saturated-red mask (R / (R + G + B) in linear light at least 0.8, and R - G - B at least 0.0625 of full scale, the ITU-R BT.1702 form). Limits: changes are taken between consecutive frames, same-direction steps merge, and the area is the share of the whole frame (the guideline's 10-degree field is not modelled)

banding.note: a staircase = a row (or column) of native luma where runs of identical values at least 6 px wide (at 1080, scaled by the frame size) are separated by 1-2 level steps, at least twice in the line. Undithered 8-bit gradients and encodes that flatten grain do this; grain, dither and noise break the plateaus up. The banded share is the fraction of the frame in those runs; warn from 4%, fail from 20%. Luma only: chroma banding is not measured

safezones.note: plan mode is type/safezones.js lintRect (0.5 px tolerance). Without boxes: a candidate is a block of strong edges (|step| >= 56 levels) that closes horizontally into a line 12-300 px tall at 1080 (width at least 1.8 x height and 40 px), 4-50% edge density, at least 4 edge runs on its middle rows and a 3:1 luma ratio between its own P95 and P5. It counts when it persists at the same place (IoU 0.6) on 2 samples taken 0.5 s apart; it fails when 50% of its area or more is outside the safe rectangle, warns from 15%. A heuristic: it cannot read, so in-scene text and graphics in the bands count too (frame-design keeps faces and key text out of the bottom 35% for the same reason)

readability.note: sizes are px at the 1080 reference (the shorter frame side; the table of frame-design and lintCaptionStyle) and are floors. The phone floor is the wide read-line floor (48 px at 1080) rendered on a 360 px wide frame: 9 px; under 12 px (the size a tested 16:9 table needed on a phone) is a note. Contrast is the WCAG ratio between the text colour (the plan's fg, else the minority cluster of the box) and the pixels behind it, taken at the lightest and darkest background percentile on up to 3 frames of the text's time: 4.5 passes, 3.0 to 4.5 warns (frame-design: the WCAG minimums are floors on video), under 3.0 fails

scene.note: a hard cut = the mean luma difference between consecutive frames is at least 2.5% of full scale and at least 4 times the median of its 8 neighbours (floored at 0.4%), with cuts at least 0.15 s apart (core.detect_cuts)

pacing.note: the format's average shot length range and shots per 30 s come from cuts/patterns.json pace (read at run time); a plan's paceRule (aslMax, longMax: plan.mjs lintPace) is used when present. A static hold = the picture stays within 3 levels (mean) of where the hold began; a hold the plan marks is exempt; over 3.5 s warns (the interrupt ladder: something visibly changes at least every 3.5 s), over 7 s fails. Only hard cuts are detected: dissolves and in-shot motion changes are not, so a long measured shot can hold several planned beats

composition.note: bars = edge rows or columns that stay near-black (mean 16 or under, std 6 or under) on 90% of sampled frames and cover 2% or more of that side; bars that together take 15% or more of the frame fail unless the plan asks for them (plan.layers or plan.look naming bars or letterbox, plan.eyes.letterbox). The hero proxy: the centre-surround saliency of the area-scaled luma, thresholded at half its maximum; blobs (0.4% of the frame or more) holding at least half the strongest blob's mass compete with it; a warning when 30% of the key frames have a competitor. It is a proxy: it does not know what the hero is. Aspect must match the platform's accepted aspects within 1%; the shorter side 1080 passes, 720 to 1079 warns, under 720 fails (--draft waives it for an animatic)

encode.note: H.264 yuv420p with the moov atom before mdat (faststart) is the pack's master (skills/social-video, output-tools). A keyframe interval over 5 s warns and over 10 s fails: a platform re-encode keeps a long GOP, seeks and loops land far from a keyframe (a house default; x264's default of 250 frames is 8.3 s at 30 fps). Bits per pixel per frame (video bit rate / (width x height x fps)) under 0.02 warns and under 0.008 fails (house default; the pack's CRF 23 demos sit far above). Blockiness = the mean step across 8 and 16 px grid lines over the mean step elsewhere, on the small steps (12 levels or less) of native frames: 1.0 is none, 1.25 warns, 1.6 fails. HD without colour tags warns (bt709 tags are on the QA list)
